topics.summary: 2025 年声明一般允许作业使用 AI，教师可因教学目的禁止；图书馆要求遵守模块说明，广泛使用须明确许可。

claims.text: NTU’s dated 24 June 2025 statement says GenAI is generally permitted in assignments, but professors may prohibit it for specific pedagogical reasons communicated to students. Students are expected to declare use and how it was used, and remain responsible for accuracy and citations. This is a dated institutional statement, not the complete current internal teaching policy or permission for every assessment.

evidence.quote: NTU’s policy is that in general, students are allowed to use Gen AI in their assignments. Many Schools across STEM and non-STEM disciplines, in medicine, and at NIE, are already using AI as part of learning. Students are expected to declare any use of AI, and how they are being used. When using AI, students are ultimately responsible for the content generated. They must ensure factual accuracy and cite all sources properly. Some professors may prohibit Gen AI for certain assignments for specific pedagogical reasons. In such cases, the reason for disallowing it is clearly communicated to students.
evidence.title: Comment on the use of AI in education | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: Official statement, 24 June 2025; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 9338:9941

claims.text: NTU Library instructs students to disclose AI-tool use in their submissions and follow their module’s AI-use policy and instructor guidance. evidence.quote: Use AI tools to support tasks such as brainstorming, outlining, or checking grammar, but ensure you disclose their use in your submissions. evidence.location: Key Points on Ethical AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 2828:3123

evidence.quote: When using AI for assignments (e.g., grammar checks, copyediting, or idea generation), adhere to the specific guidelines set by your instructor, as expectations may vary by module and discipline. To uphold academic integrity, you must always provide proper citations for all sources used, including AI‑generated content.

claims.text: For some assignments, instructors may require AI process records. NTU Library’s tracking template may be used or adapted when record-keeping is required or recommended, following the instructor’s format and level of detail.

claims.text: In research, confidential or sensitive information and personal data must not be uploaded to external GenAI platforms unless all applicable conditions are met: compliance with relevant laws and institutional policies; access restricted to authorised study members; no retention of the data in or by the GenAI; and, where applicable, explicit written permission from the data owner or agreement to that GenAI use in the Research Collaboration Agreement.

evidence.quote: Any confidential or sensitive information, and/or personal data must not be uploaded to any external GenAI software, system, or platform unless: The activity does not contravene any applicable laws, regulations, or institutional policies; Access to the GenAI is controlled and restricted to only authorised study members involved in the research; The data is not retained in or by the GenAI; and Where applicable, written permission has been explicitly provided by the data owner, or the use of such GenAI has been agreed upon in the Research Collaboration Agreement (RCA).
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: §4 Data Privacy & Confidentiality; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 6791:7364

claims.claimText: NTU’s dated 24 June 2025 statement says GenAI is generally permitted in assignments, but professors may prohibit it for specific pedagogical reasons communicated to students. Students are expected to declare use and how it was used, and remain responsible for accuracy and citations. This is a dated institutional statement, not the complete current internal teaching policy or permission for every assessment.
claims.claimValue: NTU’s dated 24 June 2025 statement says GenAI is generally permitted in assignments, but professors may prohibit it for specific pedagogical reasons communicated to students. Students are expected to declare use and how it was used, and remain responsible for accuracy and citations. This is a dated institutional statement, not the complete current internal teaching policy or permission for every assessment.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: NTU’s policy is that in general, students are allowed to use Gen AI in their assignments. Many Schools across STEM and non-STEM disciplines, in medicine, and at NIE, are already using AI as part of learning. Students are expected to declare any use of AI, and how they are being used. When using AI, students are ultimately responsible for the content generated. They must ensure factual accuracy and cite all sources properly. Some professors may prohibit Gen AI for certain assignments for specific pedagogical reasons. In such cases, the reason for disallowing it is clearly communicated to students.
evidence.snippetLocation: Official statement, 24 June 2025; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 9338:9941

approved_tools.en: NTU announced Google AI tools for undergraduates from August 2026; NALA tutors are deployed by educators. Personal account access and costs were not tested. Access does not grant assessment permission.
approved_tools.zh: 公告面向本科生提供 Google AI 工具，NALA 由教师部署；个人开通与费用未实测，工具开放不代表考核许可。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Undergraduate announcement and educator-deployed course tutors.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

research_publication.en: Acknowledge research use beyond basic spelling/grammar checks, retain human authorship and follow stricter recipient rules. Label and document AI visuals; experimental images have explicit methodology exceptions, not permission to fabricate results.
research_publication.zh: 超出拼写语法检查的科研使用应注明，保留人类作者并遵循更严格的接收方规则；图像须标注和记录，方法例外不允许伪造结果。
research_publication.meaningEn: Research proposals, scholarly outputs and theses; original should/must wording remains in evidence.
research_publication.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

academic_integrity.en: Misrepresenting AI work is academic misconduct in the Library’s handbook summary. Research plagiarism and research-misconduct referral have their own conditions; referral is not guilt or an automatic sanction.
academic_integrity.zh: 图书馆手册摘要将冒充原创视为不端；科研剽窃与移交流程另有条件，移交不等于定罪或自动处分。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Public Library summary and separately scoped research misconduct procedure.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 仅适用于相应来源列明的对象、活动与条件；完整英文说明保留如下。

teaching_guidance.en: Consult instructor and assignment guidance before using AI. Extensive AI involvement requires explicit instructor permission under the Library guidance.
teaching_guidance.zh: 按教师及任务说明使用；图书馆要求广泛 AI 参与须获教师明确许可。
teaching_guidance.meaningEn: Current public Library guidance; full internal teaching policy not obtained.
teaching_guidance.meaningZh: 仅适用于相应来源列明的对象、活动与条件；完整英文说明保留如下。

security_procurement.en: Research data conditions are explicit. The obtained public sources do not establish a complete university-wide procurement process or approval of every service for protected data.
security_procurement.zh: 研究数据保护有明确条件；公开来源不足以建立完整全校采购流程或所有服务的受保护数据批准。
security_procurement.meaningEn: Research data conditions; wider procurement evidence remains incomplete.
security_procurement.meaningZh: 仅适用于相应来源列明的对象、活动与条件；完整英文说明保留如下。

topicBasis.coursework: NTU’s 2025 statement generally permits assignment AI use, with teacher prohibitions for pedagogical reasons. Current Library guidance requires module instructions and explicit permission for extensive use.
topicBasis.exams: Do not access AI during exams where external resources are forbidden. Check the exact examination instructions; open-resource exams do not automatically authorise AI.
topicBasis.disclosure: Disclose AI assistance in submissions and follow module requirements. Detailed prompt/output records and the format depend on the instructor; thesis submissions have a separate Statement of Originality requirement.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Do not upload protected research data to external GenAI unless legal, restricted-access and no-retention conditions are met, plus owner permission where applicable or RCA agreement. The RCA route does not waive the other safeguards.
topicBasis.approved_tools: NTU announced Google AI tools for undergraduates from August 2026; NALA tutors are deployed by educators. Personal account access and costs were not tested. Access does not grant assessment permission.
topicBasis.research_publication: Acknowledge research use beyond basic spelling/grammar checks, retain human authorship and follow stricter recipient rules. Label and document AI visuals; experimental images have explicit methodology exceptions, not permission to fabricate results.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Misrepresenting AI work is academic misconduct in the Library’s handbook summary. Research plagiarism and research-misconduct referral have their own conditions; referral is not guilt or an automatic sanction.
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Consult instructor and assignment guidance before using AI. Extensive AI involvement requires explicit instructor permission under the Library guidance.
topicBasis.security_procurement: Research data conditions are explicit. The obtained public sources do not establish a complete university-wide procurement process or approval of every service for protected data.

do.en: Check module instructions and obtain permission for extensive AI involvement.
do.zh: 核对模块说明；广泛使用须获明确许可。

do.en: Follow the instructor’s disclosure and process-record requirements.
do.zh: 按教师要求披露并保留所需过程记录。

do.en: Label and document AI-generated research visuals.
do.zh: 标注并记录 AI 生成研究视觉材料。

dont.en: Do not access AI in exams that forbid external resources.
dont.zh: 禁止外部资源的考试不得访问 AI。

dont.en: Do not treat RCA authorization as waiving other research-data safeguards.
dont.zh: 不要把 RCA 授权当作豁免其他数据保护条件。

dont.en: Do not fabricate experimental results using AI images.
dont.zh: 不得以 AI 图像伪造实验结果。

clm-ntu-ai-disclosure-submissions.text: NTU Library instructs students to disclose AI-tool use in their submissions and follow their module’s AI-use policy and instructor guidance. The required level of documentation and disclosure format depend on the assignment and instructor’s expectations; detailed prompt-and-output records and a particular declaration form are not universal requirements.

evidence.quote: Use AI tools to support tasks such as brainstorming, outlining, or checking grammar, but ensure you disclose their use in your submissions. Always refer to your module's AI use policy and seek guidance from your instructor regarding specific expectations for acceptable AI usage in your courses.
evidence.location: Key Points on Ethical AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 2828:3123

evidence.quote: When using AI for assignments (e.g., grammar checks, copyediting, or idea generation), adhere to the specific guidelines set by your instructor, as expectations may vary by module and discipline. This may include documenting your AI use, completing a “ Declaration on GAI Use ,” or disclosing AI contributions where required. To uphold academic integrity, you must always provide proper citations for all sources used, including AI‑generated content.
evidence.location: Purpose of Documenting, Disclosing and Citing AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 674:1124

clm-ntu-exam-external-resources-restrict.text: NTU Library instructs students not to access AI tools during examinations when external resources are not permitted. This condition does not establish either a ban in every exam or automatic AI permission in open-resource exams.

evidence.quote: Follow Exam Protocols. Do not access AI tools during examinations when external resources are not permitted to maintain fair testing conditions.
evidence.location: Consult, Follow Exam Protocols; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 722:866

clm-ntu-extensive-ai-instructor-permissi.text: NTU Library instructs students to obtain explicit instructor permission for more extensive AI involvement, such as generating source materials or enhancing visuals.

evidence.quote: Obtain explicit permission from your instructor for more extensive AI involvement, such as generating source materials or enhancing visuals.
evidence.location: Key Points on Ethical AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 3124:3264

clm-ntu-genai-data-privacy.text: In research, confidential or sensitive information and personal data must not be uploaded to external GenAI platforms unless all applicable conditions are met: compliance with relevant laws and institutional policies; access restricted to authorised study members; no retention of the data in or by the GenAI; and, where applicable, explicit written permission from the data owner or agreement to that GenAI use in the Research Collaboration Agreement.

evidence.quote: Any confidential or sensitive information, and/or personal data must not be uploaded to any external GenAI software, system, or platform unless: The activity does not contravene any applicable laws, regulations, or institutional policies; Access to the GenAI is controlled and restricted to only authorised study members involved in the research; The data is not retained in or by the GenAI; and Where applicable, written permission has been explicitly provided by the data owner, or the use of such GenAI has been agreed upon in the Research Collaboration Agreement (RCA).
evidence.location: §4 Data Privacy & Confidentiality; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 6791:7364

clm-ntu-research-experimental-images.text: AI-generated research visuals must not be presented as actual experimental data unless AI or AI-assisted tools are an essential component of the research design and/or methodology. Using AI to fabricate images resembling experimental results constitutes serious research misconduct.

evidence.quote: AI-generated images, figures and videos must not be presented as actual experimental data unless AI (or AI-assisted) tools are an essential component of the research design and/or methodology. The use of AI to fabricate images to resemble experimental results constitutes serious research misconduct.
evidence.location: §3(ii); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 5691:5991

clm-ntu-research-misconduct-referral.text: The Vice President (Research) reviews the RIO preliminary report and may take appropriate action, decide whether to invite the Provost to appoint a COI for faculty/research staff, or decide whether to refer a student to the Board of Discipline. This is a research-misconduct process, not an automatic AI penalty or a finding of guilt.

evidence.quote: 4.4.1 The Vice President (Research) shall review the preliminary investigation report from the RIO, who will then take appropriate action (especially in relation to research staff), or decide whether to invite the Provost to appoint a COI to consider the Allegation/ Complaint under the Framework for Investigation and Disciplinary Proceedings for Faculty and Research Staff, or if the Respondent is a student, decide whether to refer to the Board of Discipline, or take any other appropriate action.
evidence.location: Research misconduct procedures §4.4.1; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 15628:16128

clm-ntu-research-visual-labelling.text: NTU requires AI-generated research images, figures and videos to be clearly labelled and the methods, tools and parameters documented sufficiently for reproducibility.

evidence.quote: All AI-generated images, figures, and videos must be clearly labelled as such. Researchers are required to document the methods, tools, and parameters used to generate these visuals in sufficient detail to ensure reproducibility.
evidence.location: §3(i); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 5457:5686
